concept: DIRECTOR A - "A day in the haunted office" (9:16, ~93 s). We approach the mansion through a moonlit, fogged forest, the house looms under a lightning hit, and the title lands as we push through the door ajar. A flash match-cuts the mansion door to the real office door: webbed glass, purple HALLOWEEN tape, a pale figure approaching through the lobby. Inside, the camera creeps over the decor (crystal ball, red-eyed skeleton spider, grinning pumpkin), finds Bob Ross mixing paint, who looks up at us on a lightning strike, then a lone figure by the autumn window, and the fog machine swallows the room. The mad doctor breaks it with "Y'all look scary" and his laugh - the flip from dread to party. The noon costume reveals run chronologically and on the beat: the Pennywise clown and her balloons, the trio stare and scream face, Luigi's dance pose, the veiled widow, Wilma on the phone, the alien, the duck wing-flap, Bob Ross deadpan, the hippie's peace sign, the leopard-onesie monster lunge. The witch's claw-reach is placed on the track's built-in dead stop (47.7-49.9 s) with lightning in the silence, and the groove slams back on her glam pose. Group portraits and the afternoon workshop ride the track's sparse breakdown (slow push-ins, a burst-twin stutter, lunch, the witch silhouette against red trees, the "summoning" presenter), the afro-wig strut with "It's the curls, isn't it?" leads into the finale, and the five-person crew goes from calm pose to monster poses on a flash. Endcard on the mansion staircase: HAPPY HALLOWEEN / 22 PROPERTIES - ONE HAUNTED HOUSE. Teal/blue night grade throughout, fog on every shot (heaviest on plates, threshold and fog-machine beats), handheld jitter on stills, grain, flicker on the dread shots; orange (pumpkins, wig, pom-poms, autumn glass) stays as the warm accent.
notes: v3 changes from QA: TV bank-login screen masked on 115920/115955 (rembg person mask keeps people sharp); 120001 dropped (duplicate of 115955, same screen); 145423 cut (unflattering, over-covered); Chuckie gets a two-shot from 123232; pom-pom burst 122923 -> 122925; 104630 cropped to the duck; 131033 -> 131030 (no faces); witch claw pinned to end on the groove return (track 50.37 s); clips that would run out now slow down instead of freezing; cooler footage grade, lifted forest plate, cold lightning, endcard fade-out, edge-safety crop, fixed fog generator. Exclusions unchanged: 122047, 123050, 123129 and the flyer are never used. MUSIC: Bump_in_the_Night measured at ~107 bpm (beat 0.56 s, bar 2.24 s), a funk-swing groove in the Thriller register; Graveyard_Shift measured ~70 bpm, slower and darker, less party. Start at 0 s because render_v.py begins the groove at the first non-plate shot (11.0 s) and the 111-s track then maps onto the body like a score: full groove under the costume reveals (footage 0-47 s), the track's built-in DEAD STOP at track 47.7-49.9 s lands on shot 27 (witch claw-reach, footage 47.2-49.7, lightning hit at ~48.3 in the silence), the sparse breakdown at track 59-73 s carries the portraits/afternoon shots 32-39 (burst-twin stutter and slow push-ins; the "It's the curls, isn't it?" line at footage ~71-73 sits in that thin bed and reads clearly), and the finale at track 74-108 s returns exactly on the crew photo (shot 40) and runs under the endcard; the renderer's 3-s fade-out ends it before the track's natural stop at 108 s. Measured 1-s RMS is in the session log if the editor wants to nudge in/out points. The intro drone (Long_Note_Two) covers only the three plates (11.0 s) by renderer design, so the dread is carried visually in footage shots 4-13 (slow push-ins, heavy fog, flicker, lightning on the spider eyes and on Bob Ross's look-up); accept that the groove starts under the threshold door - it gives the creep momentum rather than fighting it. TIMING: intro 11.0 s (title text fades in at 7.1 s overall, text2 at 7.7 s), footage 77.4 s, endcard 4.5 s, total 92.9 s before beat snapping (renderer snaps cut points to beats within 0.35 s, so expect 92-94 s). Transition flashes only at section changes (title, threshold, first costume, crew monster poses); mid-shot lightning fx on 4 shots (mansion, spider eyes, Bob Ross eyes, witch claw); glitch jolts on 2 (mad doctor stinger, clown scream face); fadeblack only on shot 1 and the endcard. Nat sound on exactly 3 videos: 115830 "Y'all look scary" + laugh, 120331 the leopard-onesie laugh (operator's "There you go, that's perfect" is also in it - harmless; mute if the editor prefers), 145759 "It's the curls, isn't it?". PRIVACY/EXCLUSIONS: 20261028_122047.mp4 not used at all (no audio, no visuals); flyer PNG skipped; 103009/103016/103507/103512 skipped (laptop screens with documents, backs of heads); 145404 skipped (renderer cannot crop to the top half, and the full frame is weak). The wall TV behind the clown/trio (shots 15, 16, 17) shows a generic two-factor-authentication web page with no credentials; the teal grade, vignette and fog knock it back, but the editor should verify it is illegible on the 1080p master and add a darker upper-right vignette if not. 120054 shows the orange "No Tricks Just Results" agenda flyer - event decor, fine. CHRONOLOGY: strictly in order except Bob Ross 10:31 stills placed inside the 10:35 decor pass (same "arrivals" beat) and 145818 (14:58:18) placed 19 s ahead of the 145759 strut so the strut leads into the finale. CROPS: landscape sources 103620 and 103606 center, 142125 left (witch + grey window); all other sources are native 9:16. Photo src values are bare filenames in src/ (the reviewer's thumbs paths were normalized). If runtime must shrink, drop in this order: 123248 stutter, 103606 pumpkin, 131033 lunch, 120049 widow, 145818. The 120/240 fps clips (115830, 120049, 145425, 145759) could be conformed to slow-motion in a later pass; the current renderer has no speed control so they are cut 1:1.

shots.why: Open from black on the moonlit forest path: the Thriller walk toward the house, drone and heavy fog.
The mansion looms past the iron gate; a lightning hit at ~1.4 s lights the facade and the one lit window.
Push through the door ajar as the title lands (text at 7.1 s overall), warm light leaking from inside.
Match-cut mansion door to the real office door: webbed glass, purple HALLOWEEN tape, a pale figure approaching through the lobby.
Decor detail: the dark crystal-ball dome on black cloth, the steadiest beat of the decor pan, fortune-teller dread.
Decor detail: the skeleton spider, window centred on its red-eyed head so the lightning lands on the eyes.
Decor detail: the tinsel jack-o'-lantern grin; flicker reads as a guttering candle.
Bob Ross head down mixing paint, unaware of the camera: the first inhabitant of the house.
Two-frame beat: he looks straight into the lens on a lightning strike.
Lone figure at the window past the foreground pumpkin; the autumn glass goes blue under the night grade.
Hero fog beat: real fog-machine haze rolls over the table toward the costumed crowd; the fog loop stacks on the practical smoke.
The room swallowed in smoke, chick onesie standing in it, exit sign glowing red.
The duck onesie alone in the fog-machine haze in front of the orange credenza (pre-cropped: the seated colleague stays out of frame).
The mad doctor breaks the dread: 'Y'all look scary' and his laugh, the flip from haunted house to party; cut before the camera drifts off him.
Pennywise beat: the clown gazes up at her balloons as the camera pushes in, then turns and smirks at us; the TV behind sits under grade and fog.
Trio portrait, slow push on the clown's cold stare between Luigi and the doctor.
Luigi hits a fists-up dance pose 1.2 s in, backlit by the window: the groove made flesh.
The veiled Victorian widow waves hello through her polka-dot veil.
Wilma takes a call and looks up grinning: the call is coming from inside the house.
Toy Story alien, three eyes above her head, the leopard onesie gesturing behind her.
Duck hood drop and wing flap, the comedy beat of the day; arms-wide at 2.4 s lands near a downbeat.
Decor detail: the ghost-face bucket of candy, a quick treats insert to reset the eye.
Bob Ross, brush poised, deadpan at the lens; a hard cut makes the stare funny.
The afro-and-blue-shades hippie flashes a peace sign from his chair: his introduction before the afternoon strut.
Leopard onesie lunges with monster claws then cracks up; her laugh under the music is the second bite, Cruella and balloons behind.
The witch beckons with a long-nailed claw inside the track's dead stop; lightning in the silence, and the cut lands exactly on the groove's return.
The groove slams back on her over-the-shoulder glam pose, red heel kicked up; drift right-to-left down the hallway.
Decor detail: a table of ghost-print goodie bags, the ghosts lyric moment.
Quartet portrait that holds all four in 9:16: Bob Ross painting, leopard onesie, witch, chick in profile.
Pom-pom team, first frame of the burst: everyone smiling at the lens.
Burst twin: push in on the orange pom-poms, the warm accent against the teal.
Pumpkin goodie bags in the foreground, the hippie/Wilma/top-hat/Chuckie lineup behind; push from bags up to faces as the breakdown starts.
Chuckie Finster and the top-hat widow, full-length two-shot, both smiling at the lens.
Lunch: the buffet trays and a plate of pasta, the house feeds its guests (no faces).
Witch silhouette against grey glass and red trees, the most haunted natural image in the set; left crop, fog on the window.
Her arm rises overhead like a summoning, bare branches behind; steady, well lit.
Wilma, the top hat and the hippie at the team flip charts; pull reveals the glitter pumpkin in the foreground.
The afro-wig strut past camera under the balloons with 'It's the curls, isn't it?', ending on the two-shot with Wilma laughing.
The crew: five in a row at the autumn window, red and black balloons, calm pose as the finale groove returns.
Lightning flash to the same five in monster poses: roar, raised balloon, peace signs; the laugh button.
Deeper into the house: the candlelit staircase hall carries the sign-off and the company line as the groove fades.
